explanation.value: Keep a preallocated array of length capacity and an integer size that says how much of it is used. A write is processed in slices: take as many bytes as fit (the smaller of the free space and the remaining input), copy them in, advance, and if the buffer is now full, drain it to the sink and reset size to zero. Draining appends the buffered bytes to this call's output list (and, when a sink object was given, calls its write for each byte). flush drains only when size is positive. Each input byte is copied once into the buffer and once out, so a write costs time proportional to its length.

explanation.value: Allocate buffer = [0]*capacity and size = 0. In write, loop while input remains: take = min(capacity - size, remaining), copy that slice into buffer[size:size+take], advance size and the input index, and drain if size == capacity. _drain appends buffer[0:size] to the call's output list, forwards each byte to an optional sink, and resets size. flush creates an output list and drains only when size > 0.
